cause: after 4 was concluded positive and 13, 14 filed under it

6-add-random-unjudged-pictures-as-backgr.line: Cheap and offline on idea 4's harness, and it picks which classifier idea 5 puts in front of a person.

why.impact: Idea 4 found the gain comes from using the rejects; plain background negatives are the next step in the same direction and change what idea 5 tests.
why.odds: Review rejects are near-misses, so background negatives plausibly help the library-wide top 100, but a held-out test alone may not show it.
why.path: Idea 4's harness and exported data are ready; idea 5 should use whichever variant wins.

14-break-the-shipped-neighbour-vote-s-ti.line: Cheap and offline: if the shipped vote just needs its ties broken or rejects counted, that may be the whole fix #2678 needs.

why.impact: A small change to the shipped source is easier to ship than a new classifier, and it sets the baseline idea 5 compares against.
why.odds: Idea 4's judged-only vote, which counts rejects as negatives, already tied the classifier on every tag, so this is very likely to close the gap.
why.path: Runs on idea 4's harness now; its winner should be the vote list in idea 5.

10-add-a-random-batch-to-the-person-judg.line: Run inside idea 5's blind review: idea 4's win is on hand-picked pictures, and only a random batch shows whether it holds on the open library.

why.impact: Idea 2 found a strong model confirming new pictures at the random rate, so this control decides whether idea 5's numbers mean anything.
why.odds: Adding a random batch to a review is easy and almost certain to give a usable baseline.
why.path: Shares idea 5's review, so it sits just before it.

13-put-a-neighbour-vote-over-judged-pict.line: Run inside idea 5's blind review: the judged-only vote tied the classifier in idea 4, and only new pictures can tell which one to ship.

why.impact: It decides whether #2678 ships a classifier or a simpler vote.
why.odds: Adding a third list to the same review is easy and gives an answer either way.
why.path: Shares idea 5's review; should use idea 14's version of the vote if that wins.

5-a-person-judges-the-classifier-s-top-1.line: The deciding test, with a random batch (10) and the judged-only vote (13) in the same blind review.

why.impact: Confirms on unjudged pictures are the issue's own success measure.
why.odds: Idea 4 beat the shipped vote by 20-30 points in the top 50 on content tags like jewelry and teeth, but only among reviewed pictures, and idea 2 warns such wins can vanish on new ones.
why.path: Should use the winners of ideas 6 and 14 and carry ideas 10 and 13.

9-a-stronger-picture-embedding-for-tags-.line: Its trigger has happened: in idea 4 every method sat near chance on defect tags while content tags worked.

why.impact: It would open fine-grained tags, but those are mostly the anomaly tagger's own, and a larger embedding costs storage and a library pass.
why.odds: Idea 1's DINOv3 probe put 56 to 74 true positives in its top 100 for defect tags, but with about 1,200 labels rather than 100.
why.path: Can run now on idea 4's harness; nothing waits on it.

7-combine-the-classifier-and-the-near-ne.line: Weakened by idea 4: the judged-only vote tied the classifier on every tag, and idea 13's overlap count answers it for free.

why.impact: If the two rankers agree, a combination ships no better than either alone.
why.odds: Idea 4 found the classifier and the judged-only vote within each other's spread on every tag.
why.path: Nothing waits on it; idea 13 reports how much the lists overlap.

11-use-the-base-rate-thresholds-as-the-n.line: Already answered in practice: idea 4 ran the shipped near-neighbour kernel copied unchanged.

why.impact: Only a methodological check, and idea 4's report already lists the vote's coverage per tag.
why.odds: Using the shipped code is what idea 4 did.
why.path: Nothing waits on it; a candidate for closing from idea 4's report rather than a new session.

12-have-a-person-judge-the-vote-s-top-10.line: Settles idea 3's open verdict but barely touches the main question; could ride along in idea 5's review.

why.impact: It only decides which version of the shipped vote is the baseline, and idea 4 shows the bigger issue is that vote ignoring rejects.
why.odds: The two lists differ only where the old 55% bar lets fewer than 100 through, so a difference is likely only on the rarest tags.

8-pick-the-next-pictures-to-judge-by-the.line: Last: idea 2 found a held-out model's ranking no better than random, and this only speeds up a source that must work first.

why.impact: It saves verdicts but does not answer whether the classifier works.
why.odds: Idea 2 concluded negative: ranked batches confirmed at the random rate, and the score did not order positives (AUC 0.49).
